items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: I had one guy. He came out in 46, Bob Watts. ... Most of the time I had a mixed band.

ctx.x: You have any New Orleans guys out there with you? No.

I had one guy. He came out in 46, Bob Watts. What did he play? Trumpet. Most of the time I had a mixed band. Some of the time I had white Mexicans. On the last I had, nobody was in the band. But me, I had four Mexicans with myself for about three years until my job closed.
What kind of music did the Mexicans play? My kind of music. College music. American music. They were, man. They were, man.

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: I don't know who Bob played with around here... That wasn't with me. I wasn't with him.

ctx.x: And what about Bob Watts? You tell me about him coming out from Texas.
Oh, a little Bob. A little trumpet player? Yeah. Bob's a nice little trumpet player.

items.title: Bob Watts Interview, 1963-02-28
items.q: Alfred Williams right here. He used to tell me and I thought I couldn't quit and I never touched it no more.

ctx.x: We got the reel three Bob Watson, it's February this time. February the 28th, 1963 and we were getting to El Paso and you would have sent them a telegram there.

Yeah. Well, Guy Moe, they sent it, as I said before, a couple of days, two or three days they sent me what I asked for so I went on up there, see, and then I played, oh I must have worked with them about four or five months, see. I worked there with them about four or five months. And then I don't know, I got to the place where I just wanted to get up a little group of my own, you know. I got in touch with some fellas there, see. Tiny Joe, that was a booker, a very, about 350 pound colored fella. Yeah. But he was…
Yeah, yeah, yeah. But he didn't have the job, eh? Did he have the job for the boys? Oh yeah. He had it.
